title: GreySkull program review
summary: NH reviews the GreySkull LP novice program, which alternates bench and press, adds curls and weighted chins, and uses 2x5 plus a 5+ AMRAP set. He calls it an improvement on Starting Strength but still a minimalist skeleton: bench volume swings week to week, lift order is poor, the Friday mirrors the Monday, and there is no direct work for abs, traps, delts or calves. He gives fixes and suggests using it as a base for your own program.
claims: GreySkull is a powerlifting-style novice program built as an improvement on Starting Strength, but it stays close to its parent
A program stands on its own; you judge it by its variables, not by its author
Fix the vague 2x5 plus 5+ scheme with an evolving set/rep range or 3x5 followed by 2-3 back-off sets
Curls for 2x10-15 encourage chasing the pump; do 3-4 sets of 6-10 or 8-12 instead
Superset curls with the press to save time; it won't hurt your pressing
Squats should open the day because they are the most demanding lift, not come after pressing and curls
Alternating bench and press means some weeks have only one bench day, so tonnage swings randomly and novices won't know why strength stalls
Benching flat all the time gives many people shoulder problems; for looks, push-ups or dumbbell bench work as well
Weighted chins at 2x6-8 are a good addition, and loading only after 6-8 clean bodyweight chins is the right rule
Power cleans have no place in a novice program and add nothing for hypertrophy
Do the deadlift first in the session, then 3x3 back-off sets
Two identical days in a program are unnecessary; rotate in variations such as dumbbell bench, preacher curls or pause squats
The program lacks direct ab, trap, shoulder, calf and long-head triceps work
To modify GreySkull, add bodyweight pull-ups on another day, ab isolation at the end of sessions, shrugs after deadlifts (3-4 sets), and lateral raises
Run it for 3-6 months with the fixes, then use it as a skeleton to write your own program
Novices make gains on almost any program
exercises: load only after 6-8 clean bodyweight reps
vertical pull missing from Starting Strength
not suited to beginners; pointless for hypertrophy
lower the weight after deadlifts, 3-4 sets
the program has no direct shoulder isolation
